entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Amenemhet VI was the pharaoh of the early Thirteenth Dynasty of ancient Egypt, ruling from approximately 1810 to 1795 BCE. He is known for his military campaigns against the Hyksos in northern Egypt and his efforts to restore Egyptian power and influence.

His reign was marked by a series of conflicts with neighboring kingdoms, including the Mitanni and the Hittites. Amenemhet VI also oversaw significant architectural projects, including the construction of several temples and monuments at Thebes and Memphis.

Despite his military successes, Amenemhet VI's reign ultimately ended in failure, as he was defeated by the Hyksos and eventually deposed. However, his legacy continued to shape Egyptian history for centuries to come.

The discovery of his tomb has provided valuable insights into the culture and politics of ancient Egypt during this period, shedding light on the daily lives of Egyptians during this time.
